chief_complaint: painless firm lump in upper outer quadrant of breast
hpi_details: A 77-year-old male presents to the clinic with painless firm lump in upper outer quadrant of breast. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: He thinks the lump is merely a harmless fatty deposit or scar tissue from bumping his chest against a fence post while working outside.
concerns: He is worried that this lump is an aggressive breast cancer and feels embarrassed about facing painful surgery in an area men don't expect to have checked.
expectations: He hopes to have an ultrasound today to verify that it is benign so he can avoid an invasive procedure.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Breast Cancer (suspicious mass, pending biopsy) evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Breast Cancer (suspicious mass, pending biopsy) is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Breast Cancer: Order mammogram and ultrasound, refer for core needle biopsy, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

teaching.one_liner: A painless, firm lump in the breast — especially in the upper outer quadrant, where most breast cancers arise — that requires imaging and biopsy to confirm malignancy.
red_flags: Skin dimpling, nipple retraction, or axillary lymphadenopathy — suggests more advanced disease

must_ask.say: When did you first notice the lump?
Is it firm, and does it move when you press on it?
Any dimpling, puckering, or nipple changes?
Have you felt anything in your armpit?
Does breast cancer run in your family?

history.answer: I came in because I noticed a hard lump in my left breast about three weeks ago, and it seems to be getting bigger.
I first noticed it about three weeks ago while I was washing up in the shower, and it definitely wasn't there before.
It is located in the upper outer area of my left breast, just a single firm lump, and there is nothing on the right side.
It started out about the size of a small marble, but over the last couple of weeks it has gradually grown larger and firmer.
No, it doesn't hurt at all, even when I press directly on it.
I haven't seen any dimpling, puckering, redness, or orange-peel texture on the skin over my breast.
My nipple looks completely normal with no retraction, pulling inward, or eczema-like scaling.
No, there has been no fluid, blood, or discharge coming from my nipples.
I tried feeling under my armpits, and I didn't feel any swollen glands or lumps there.
No, I haven't had any fevers or chills, and my chest has not felt hot or red.
Yes, I have been feeling unusually tired and run-down lately, which isn't like me.
My appetite has been fairly normal, and I haven't noticed any unintentional weight loss.
No, I don't have any bone pain or aching in my back or hips.
No, I haven't had any cough, shortness of breath, or trouble breathing.
No, I have never injured my chest, and I have never had any procedures or biopsies done on my breasts.
I've never had any breast disease before, and I've never received radiation therapy to my chest.
No, I have never taken estrogen, testosterone, or any other hormone medications.
No, I'm not taking any steroids, prostate medications, or anti-androgen treatments.
I have never had hepatitis, cirrhosis, or any liver problems, and I only drink alcohol very rarely.
No, I haven't had any testicular pain, swelling, or changes in my sex drive.
I figured it was just a harmless fatty bump or some scar tissue from when I banged my chest against a fence post a few weeks ago.
I'm embarrassed to even have a lump there, but I'm deeply worried it could be an aggressive cancer that requires major surgery.
I was hoping you could do an ultrasound today to prove it's harmless so I don't have to go through surgery.
I have generally been very healthy and have no history of chronic illnesses like hypertension or diabetes.
I have never had any surgeries or hospital admissions in my life.
I do not take any prescription medications, over-the-counter drugs, or herbal supplements.
No, I don't have any allergies to medications or anything else.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used tobacco products.
I only drink socially, maybe a single beer once or twice a month at most.
I am a retired accountant, and I currently live at home with my wife.
No one in my family has ever had breast cancer, ovarian cancer, or any other malignancy that I know of.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 124/78 mmHg, heart rate 72/min, respiratory rate 16/min, body temperature 36.6°C, SpO2 98% on room air.
Elderly gentleman in no acute distress, looking slightly fatigued but alert, cooperative, and comfortable at rest.
Palpable 2 cm firm, non-tender, fixed mass in the upper outer quadrant of the left breast; no skin dimpling, peau d'orange, nipple retraction, discharge, or palpable axillary lymphadenopathy.
No palpable cervical or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy.
Symmetric chest wall expansion without chest wall tenderness or rib deformities.
Clear breath sounds bilaterally with no crackles, wheezes, or rhonchi.
Regular rate and rhythm with normal S1 and S2; no murmurs, gallops, or friction rubs.
Soft, non-tender abdomen with no distension, guarding, or rigidity.
No hepatomegaly or splenomegaly palpable; normal liver span.
No jaundice, spider angiomas, palmar erythema, or unusual skin lesions.
Normal male external genitalia with symmetric, non-tender testes and no palpable scrotal masses or atrophy.
